title: Article 116 — Votes on account, votes of credit and exceptional grants

content.overview: Article 116 empowers the House of the People to make grants in advance (votes on account) pending completion of the procedure for voting grants and passing the Appropriation Act; to make grants for meeting unexpected demands (votes of credit) when ordinary procedure is not practicable due to magnitude or indefinite character; and to make exceptional grants that form no part of the current service of any financial year. Parliament has power to authorise by law withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund for such grants.
content.glance: LS may make: votes on account (advance grants); votes of credit (unexpected demands); exceptional grants. Parliament may authorise withdrawal by law.
content.study:
Article 116 provides flexibility for:
1. Votes on account — advance grants before the full budget process is complete.
2. Votes of credit — unexpected demands when ordinary process is impracticable.
3. Exceptional grants — not part of the current service of any financial year.

Parliament may authorise by law the withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund for the purposes for which such grants are made.

Examination: three types; LS power; parliamentary law for withdrawal.

sections.heading: Three types
sections.body:
1. Votes on account: advance grants pending full procedure.
2. Votes of credit: unexpected demands (magnitude/indefinite character).
3. Exceptional grants: not part of current service of any financial year.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are votes on account and votes of credit under Article 116?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 116, the House of the People may make grants in advance (votes on account) in respect of the estimated expenditure for part of a financial year pending completion of the grant-voting and Appropriation Act procedure; grants to meet unexpected demands (votes of credit) when on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of the service the demand cannot be stated with detail required in ordinary procedure; and exceptional grants which form no part of the current service of any financial year. Parliament may authorise by law withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund for these purposes.
